title: Peter Shane on Bennett and the procedural stage
shortTitle: Peter Shane on Bennett and the procedural stage
summary: The supplied fragment treats Bennett as evidence against the harshest reading of Lujan while acknowledging the different burdens at dismissal and summary judgment.
notes:
The assigned page begins in the middle of Shane’s discussion of Bennett v. Spear. The available text explains how a Fish and Wildlife Service biological opinion constrained another agency’s options and how the Bureau’s prior reservoir practice supported an inference of redress. A unanimous finding of standing in that setting suggested that indirect causation and redressability need not always be fatal.

Shane also acknowledges a substantial qualification: Bennett arose at dismissal on the complaint, while Lujan evaluated proof at summary judgment. That difference affects what the plaintiff must establish and how the comparison should be understood.
